clue.text: Doc's brewed beer is crap

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so the word before it is jumbled

blocks.note: wallop is British slang for beer

explanation.surface: A doctor's home brew gets a rude verdict from the drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallop is old British slang for beer, especially cheap mild ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for nonsense or rubbish talk, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Bird starts to apply tension overtly inside penis ring

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are the only letters wanted
the selected letters sit within the pair of words that follows

blocks.note: a slang word for the male organ
initial letters of these three words
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A sex-shop instruction for fitting a ring, worthy of Private Eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials go between the slang word and the ring-shaped letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockatoo is a crested parrot, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Randy queen vacating a throne when screwed

indicators.note: the royal leaves, so her letter departs from the words that follow
screwed up or twisted, the remaining letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A lusty monarch leaves her throne for a bit of bedroom action.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R out of A THRONE and rearrange what is left to get ON HEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal on heat is sexually receptive, and randy is slang for sexually eager, so they match.

clue.text: Adolescent's down behind, cock up

blocks.note: to fluff something is to bungle it

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a teenager's buttocks and an awkward erection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like a direction but is soft hair; a cock-up is British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumfluff is British slang for the sparse first facial hair growing on a teenage boy's face.

clue.text: Go berserk, top to bottom, for a threesome

indicators.note: letters move between the ends of this down light, rotating the word

blocks.note: to riot is to run wild

explanation.surface: Someone loses control and flips over, all for a three-way romp.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the end letter of RIOT goes up to the top to give TRIO; the setter's phrase names the swap between ends loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a group of three, which is what threesome literally means.

clue.text: Expanding operation at the front: Bush and Blair initially without balls to take on the task

indicators.note: only the first letter of each named politician is needed
without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go round the next item

blocks.note: first letters of the two leaders' names
two balls look like two round letters

explanation.surface: Bush and Blair launch a front-line war operation without the guts to do it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the Iraq invasion; the definition is a cheeky description of breast enlargement surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob job is cosmetic surgery enlarging the breasts, an operation that expands the chest.

clue.text: After book, lid taken off errant Miliband (nameless cute creature)

indicators.note: the next piece follows the first one in order
these letters are removed from the politician's surname
straying from the right path, the letters wander into a new order
without its name abbreviation, so that letter is dropped too

blocks.note: the three letters of this word are removed one by one
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A dishevelled Miliband, his top blown off after a book, is likened to something cute.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike L, I and D and then N from MILIBAND to leave MIBA, which rearranges behind B to make BAMBI.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambi is the Disney fawn, a famously sweet cartoon deer and so a cute creature.

clue.text: Prepared for assault: desirable position for a gay in Knightsbridge?

definitions.text: desirable position for a gay in Knightsbridge

blocks.note: first meaning: ready to defend oneself

blocks.clueFragment: desirable position for a gay in Knightsbridge
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: astride a soldier

explanation.surface: Seems a nudge about the soldiers of Knightsbridge barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: Knightsbridge in London is home to the Household Cavalry barracks, whose troopers are guardsmen; the joke reads the phrase as being on top of one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on guard means alert and ready to resist attack; the second sense is a smutty literal reading.

clue.text: Our columnist occasionally getting leg over and shaking up good girls

indicators.note: shaken up, the letters gathered here fall into a new arrangement

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Private Eye's own gossip columnist is said to get her leg over now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our columnist' means Private Eye's own: Glenda Slagg is its spoof tabloid columnist; 'occasionally getting leg over' is colour about her character.
explanation.definitionFit: Glenda Slagg is the magazine's long-running parody of female Fleet Street columnists, so she is its columnist.

clue.text: Schmaltz rejected to get rid of heroin problem

indicators.note: turned back, so the word is read from the end
one letter must be discarded from the result

explanation.surface: A soppy story about kicking a drug habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is an arithmetic problem set for pupils, so the words share that sense.

clue.text: Pop star, left out, likely to throw a wobbly

indicators.note: the letter for left is out, removed from the word
a tantrum puts things in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A sidelined pop diva seems liable to have a tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Kylie Minogue is the Australian singer known by first name alone, an example of a pop star.

clue.text: see 23ac.
Disgraced MP turned minor celeb and no stranger to the pits

blocks.note: first meaning: Neil, the Tory MP of cash-for-questions fame who went on to reality TV
second meaning: Lewis, the Formula One champion who makes pit stops

explanation.surface: A shamed politician reinvented as a C-list celebrity has sunk low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The pits' looks like a verdict on the MP's career; it is the motor-racing pit lane.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname is shared by Neil the ex-MP and Lewis the racing driver, each fitting one phrase.

clue.text: Not quite genuine TV presenter, one wilfully having no class

indicators.note: falling just short, the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: Ant of the TV double act Ant and Dec

explanation.surface: A fake TV host is dismissed as a deliberate yob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No class' looks like a sneer about manners; it means skipping school lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A truant deliberately stays away from school, so misses lessons or class.

clue.text: Self-conceit: can Sir Dicky miss out?

indicators.note: dicky means faulty or unsound, so the letters around it are disordered
put out of order, reinforcing the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A vain knight called Dicky wonders if he could be left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sir Dicky' reads as a title and name; dicky is British slang for unreliable or shaky.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissism is excessive admiration of oneself, the same idea as conceit about one's own worth.

clue.text: Opening of Ed Balls' centre designed for "moral erect"  – potential threat to his and some other MPs' seats?

definitions.text: potential threat to his and some other MPs' seats

indicators.note: the first letter of the leader's name is the one kept
the middle letter of the surname is the one kept
the letters are redesigned into a new shape

explanation.surface: Ed Balls, Labour MP, gets a phallic makeover that might cost him his seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is part of the jumble, not a link. Ed Balls lost his seat in 2015; voting changes could threaten MPs in marginal seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Changing the voting system could unseat sitting members, so reform of elections threatens their seats.

clue.text: VD? Make high-pitched sound, showing appreciation

blocks.note: the clap is slang for gonorrhoea
a ping is a short high ringing sound

explanation.surface: A sexually transmitted infection prompts a squeal, oddly read as applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapping hands is how an audience expresses approval or appreciation of a performance.

clue.text: Shagging Ginger or Dotty

indicators.note: dotty means crazy, so the letters go haywire

explanation.surface: A choice of bedfellow: a redhead or someone called Dotty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' looks like a woman's name paired with Ginger; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To roger is vulgar British slang for having sex with someone, as is to shag.

clue.text: Piss while holding pint – get it everywhere

indicators.note: the first word holds the next letter within it

blocks.note: a slash is British slang for urinating
P is the abbreviation for pint

explanation.surface: Peeing with a pint in hand is bound to end messily.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'have a slash' means to urinate.
explanation.definitionFit: To splash liquid is to scatter it about, getting it all over the place.

clue.text: Tabloids' dishonest, phoney operator gets chop – taken to casualty

blocks.note: to hack is to chop roughly
ER, the emergency room, is the American casualty department

explanation.surface: A crooked tabloid reporter gets the sack and lands in A&E.
explanation.walkthrough: 'phoney' puns on phone: tabloid hacking of mobile phone messages caused the 2011 scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone hacker illegally broke into voicemails for tabloid newspapers, a dishonest operator of phones.

clue.text: Assistance needed by suitor getting shagged, having grabbed English lass?

explanation.definitionFit: Legal aid is state funding for court costs, help that a litigant may need.

clue.text: see 22dn.
Hamlet-like, topless, bent over – weedy thing!
